title: Arms wide on the Rim Trail
summary: An early October evening hike on the Tahoe Rim Trail at Tahoe Meadows, near Chickadee Ridge, with Helena and Marley: a lake view through old snags, arms wide on a granite rock, a chickadee taking seed from Helena's hand, the Ophir Creek sign, a boardwalk at golden hour, and an orange sunset over Lake Tahoe from the car on the drive down.

5:42 pm. Marley watches from the dirt while she stands on the rock, arms out.
The two of us on the trail.
6:20 pm. On the boardwalk, the meadow gone gold.
6:46 pm. Orange and pink sky over Lake Tahoe.

post.title: Arms wide on the Rim Trail
post.body:
Sunday evening, early October, a hike on the Tahoe Rim Trail at Tahoe Meadows, near Chickadee Ridge. At about half past five the lake showed up between two old snags, silver-grey under a hazy sky, with a forested point reaching out into the water and the far shore stacked up behind it.

A few steps on there was a flat granite rock with a view, and Helena climbed up on it. First one arm up, then both out wide. Marley sat in the dirt in her harness and watched her the whole time. I took a lot of pictures in about five seconds.

We'd already stopped once to wait for chickadees, and around a quarter to six one came down and ate seed from Helena's hand. I had three or four come to me, but she didn't catch any of mine on camera, so you'll have to take my word for it.

Around six we were walking the trail through the pines, and I turned the camera around for a couple of selfies. Neither of us is dressed for anything serious in these. It was that kind of evening.

A quarter past six brought us to the junction post: Ophir Creek on one side, a Tahoe Rim Trail map and elevation profile on the other, and nearby a TRT Mountain Bike Advisory sign asking everyone to share this busy section and keep it safe and enjoyable. A few minutes later we were on a wooden boardwalk with the meadow gone gold and the light getting low behind the peaks.

At a quarter to seven, on the drive down, the sky over the lake went orange and pink, with the trees in black silhouette and the far mountains a dark line under it all. Helena took the picture from the car. It's a little blurry at the bottom. I kept it anyway.

What I learned: you don't need a big plan. An hour and a bit on the Rim Trail at the end of the day, a rock to stand on, and the lake does the rest.

episode.title: Arms wide on the Rim Trail
episode.script:
A little before half past five on a Sunday in October, on the Tahoe Rim Trail at Tahoe Meadows, near Chickadee Ridge, with the lake showing through two old, mossy snags.

The sky was hazy. The water below was silver, with a dark, forested point reaching out into it, and the far shore stacked up in blue behind.

Christian wasn't hiking alone. Helena was with him, and so was Marley.

***

A few minutes on, there was a flat slab of granite with a view. Helena stepped up onto it. One arm went up. Then both arms went out, wide, like she was taking in the whole basin at once.

Marley sat down in the dirt, in her harness, and watched. She didn't move. Christian took pictures, quickly, before the moment went anywhere.

***

They'd already stopped once to wait for chickadees. Around a quarter to six, one finally came down and ate seed from Helena's hand.

Christian had three or four come to him. Helena didn't catch a single one of his on camera. So his chickadees live on only in the telling.

***

Around six they were walking the trail through the pines. Soft dirt underfoot, bare trunks all around. Christian turned the camera around and caught the two of them, close together, the trail running off behind.

At a quarter past six they reached the junction post. On one side, a map and an elevation profile. On the other, a tall sign that simply said Ophir Creek. Nearby, an advisory for mountain bikers, asking everyone to share this busy section of the Rim Trail and keep it safe and enjoyable.

A few minutes later, a wooden boardwalk. The grass had turned gold, the peaks were going dark at the edges, and the light was low. One more selfie, both of them smiling.

***

Then, at a quarter to seven, on the drive down, the sky did the thing it sometimes does over Tahoe.

Bands of orange and pink across the clouds. The lake underneath, glowing the same colour. Pines in black silhouette, and a dark line of mountains on the far shore.

Helena took that one from the car. It's a little blurry at the bottom. Christian kept it.

***

No resin this time. No stones. Nothing to wire up for the lamp project.

Just an evening on the Rim Trail, a rock to stand on, and a dog who knows how to watch.
